sources_considered.why: Readable contemporary reporting on subscription/API price differences and customer responses; does not identify a causal behavioral effect.
Dated primary research identifies technical variation in token consumption, an alternative explanation requiring control.
Search results concern consumer demand and retention, rather than enterprise efficiency across billing regimes.
Search results concern subscription tier and adoption intentions; this does not directly test the claimed enterprise spending mechanism.

evidence_items.locator: Section Expensive frontier models have firms looking elsewhere
evidence_items.explanation: The report establishes a price difference consistent with weaker marginal-price signals under subscriptions. It does not measure learned inefficiency or establish the causal effect of earlier subscription use.

The study reports substantial variation in token consumption across models and repeated executions, without studying subscription-induced habits. Those technical factors complicate attributing spending problems to customer conditioning.

unresolved_gaps: No matched before-and-after customer study establishes the alleged learning effect.
No evidence separates subscription incentives from changing agent workloads, model behavior, or missing spending controls.
API list-price comparisons do not establish the amount of any below-cost subsidy.
